## Summary

This PR introduces `insights` middleware.
It is to automatically setup userToken across search calls and Insights api calls.
Once this middleware is added to `instantSearchInstance`, when user calls

```js
window.aa('setUserToken', userToken);
// or 
insightsClient('setUserToken', userToken);
```

the middleware will automatically apply the userToken to the searchParameters. Then the next search call will include this userToken.

**Stacked PRs**
1. [introduce `insights` middleware](https://github.com/algolia/instantsearch.js/pull/4446) ← current
2. [send events from hits and refinementList](https://github.com/algolia/instantsearch.js/pull/4456)
3. [implement sendEvent in all the connectors](https://github.com/algolia/instantsearch.js/pull/4463)
4. [add tests](https://github.com/algolia/instantsearch.js/pull/4464)

**examples**
- basic example: https://codesandbox.io/s/instantsearchjs-jetcz?file=/src/app.js
- with search-insights **umd**: https://codesandbox.io/s/instantsearchjs-zn81s?file=/src/app.js
- `insightsClient: false`: https://codesandbox.io/s/instantsearchjs-1igbb?file=/src/app.js
(_working example_: [esm](https://codesandbox.io/s/instantsearchjs-5qwf4?file=/src/app.js), [umd]())

```
insightsClient('setUserToken', 'def');

search.EXPERIMENTAL_use(createInsightsMiddleware({ insightsClient }));
```

In current implementation, if user sets userToken before creating the middleware, it will get ignored.
Does it make sense to you as long as it's documented? Or, should we allow user do that and somehow catch the token?

→ For more info, the reason why this doesn't work is,
`insightsClient('init', { ... })` happens when creating the middleware.
It means at the time `insightsClient('setUserToken', 'def');` is called, it's not even initialized.

@eunjae-lee Is there a use case where the Insights' `userToken` can differ from InstantSearch's? As far as I know, there's none. We could display a dev warning saying that we detected that a token was previously set, but it's ignored because of the middleware (this warning can be displayed even if the `userToken` is the same, since it's useless to set it outside of the middleware).
